display.title: Episode 511: The Mountain of Ice (Yud Shevat)
display.summary_short: On the eve of Yud Shevat, Uncle Yossi tells of the Frierdiker Rebbe's mesiras nefesh for Torah, then the story of Reb Meir of Premishlan, who walked down an icy mountain without slipping.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on the eve of Yud Shevat. Uncle Yossi explains that this is the yahrzeit of the Frierdiker Rebbe, Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn, who built a network of underground yeshivos in Soviet Russia, was arrested and sentenced to death in 1927, was saved by miracles, and in 1940 came to New York and sent scholars across America to found yeshivos. On this day we resolve to learn more Torah, do more mitzvos and give more tzedakah. After the Hakochainik march, two young siblings say the Shema in Studio 604, and everyone gives tzedakah. Story time: in Premishlan a mikvah stood atop a steep mountain whose steps froze over in winter, yet Reb Meir walked up and down them daily without slipping. Two visiting businessmen mocked the sight, tried it themselves and tumbled down. After recovering they asked his forgiveness and his secret: 'One who is tied above does not fall below.' Through Torah and mitzvos we bind ourselves to Hashem. The show ends with a listener's letter about giving tzedakah and Shabbos candle-lighting times.
display.lesson: When we tie ourselves to Hashem through Torah and mitzvos, we do not fall.

date.note: 'The evening right before Yud Shevat'; 9 Shevat 5752 was a Tuesday. Candle time 4:36 fits.

segments.title: The Mountain of Ice
segments.summary: Reb Meir of Premishlan walks down icy steps without slipping, and teaches two mocking visitors that one tied to Hashem does not fall.
